YOUR SCOPE: **conventions & architecture alignment only.** Do not review styling tokens (another agent has that) or business logic correctness (another agent has that).

Read these rule files FIRST and treat them as the standard:
- .claude/rules/conventions.md
- .claude/rules/components.md
- .claude/rules/typescript.md
- .claude/rules/overrides.md  (if it exists)
- .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md  (ONLY the sections on: "Importing an already-overridden component from a new component", "The SFCC bridge pattern", "Co-locating a component's theme file")
- AGENTS.md (Rules section: Copy-first rule, Minimal changes, Icons, Comments)

Check specifically:
1. **Import correctness** — overrideStyling.md has a critical rule: importing an already-overridden component must use a RELATIVE path, not `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`, because the resolver only runs in the real app build (not Storybook/Vitest). Check every import in the changed files for this trap. Also check for base-path imports of things that DO have local overrides.
2. **File/folder structure** — ui-kits atoms/molecules placement, camelCase folder naming, `index.tsx` convention, co-located `.css.ts`, test/story file naming (`index.test.tsx` vs `.spec`).
3. **Component contract rules** — named export matching folder name, props type naming (`XProps`), props type placement, JSDoc requirements, callback prop naming, required-vs-optional props.
4. **Container/presentational separation** — components under `overrides/app/components/` must NOT call data-fetching hooks; data fetching belongs in `pages/`. Check whether this holds. Note the documented exception for `useIntl`/`useUiCopy`.
5. **TypeScript idioms** — `any`, non-null assertions, `type` vs `interface`, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, discriminated unions where warranted. Any TS that is technically valid but odd/misleading (e.g. a prop typed as a single literal that the component internally widens).
6. **i18n / hardcoded copy** — does the project have an established pattern for user-facing microcopy in a leaf component? Look for `overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts`, `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/`, `translations/`, and how existing ui-kits components source their visible text strings. Then check whether the changed files follow it. Report any hardcoded user-facing English string.
7. **Comment quality** — AGENTS.md says don't remove existing comments, and conventions.md governs NEW comments. Assess the new comments: are any of them factually checkable claims that reference line numbers in other files (rot risk)? Verify 2-3 of the most specific such claims against the actual files and report whether they are currently accurate.
8. **Magic numbers/strings**, Australian spelling in Zimmermann-authored identifiers, `console.*` calls.

METHOD — closed loop, this matters:
- For every finding, OPEN the actual file and confirm it. Never report from the diff alone.
- Distinguish **CONFIRMED** (you read the file and the defect is definitely there) from **PLAUSIBLE** (looks wrong, couldn't fully verify).
- Where a rule has a documented exception, check whether the exception applies before calling it a violation.
- Compare against SIBLING components that already exist on this branch (other ui-kits atoms/molecules) to establish what "the established approach" actually is in practice, not just what the docs say. Cite the sibling file you compared to.

OUTPUT: A concise, ranked list. For each: `file:line` — severity (Blocker / Major / Minor / Nit) — one-sentence defect — the specific rule or sibling-precedent it violates — CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE. Then a 3-line overall verdict on conventions alignment. No preamble, no summary of what you read. Be rigorous but do not invent findings to pad the list — if something is clean, say so briefly.

## Findings (ranked)

**1. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:107,110` — Blocker** — The user-facing words `Was` and `Now` are bare JSX literals, so all 11 locales / 8 storefronts render English. Violates the in-folder sibling precedent `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:7-21`, which puts identical PDP microcopy through `intl.formatMessage` with `id: 'product_view.label.style_code'` + inline `defaultMessage`, and whose docblock (lines 34-39) explicitly rejects this exact shortcut: *"a bare literal is not the remedy for that, it just ships English to all eleven locales instead."* Verified `product_view.label.*` is a live namespace in `translations/en-GB.json`, that `style_code` is not yet extracted (so `defaultMessage`-only works with zero Tier 2 `translations/` edits), and that base SFCC already translates sale copy (`product_tile.badge.label.sale`). `useUiCopy` is *not* the right tool here — same reasoning as the sibling. — **CONFIRMED**

**2. Lint regression: 8 new `prettier/prettier` ESLint errors — Major**
`zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:47, 50, 65` · `zimmProductContent/index.tsx:45` · `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:364, 371, 373, 942`. All on lines this PR touched. Proven closed-loop: piping each file's `develop` version through `npx eslint --stdin --stdin-filename <real path>` yields **0** prettier errors; HEAD yields 8. `npm run lint` goes from clean to failing on all three files. — **CONFIRMED**

**3. `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:106-111` — Major** — No whitespace text node between the two spans, so `textContent` is `"Was $595.00Now $450.00"` — and with `aria-atomic="true"` that concatenation is exactly what AT reads. `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:60-65` hits the identical two-spans-in-a-flex-row case and solves it with an explicit `{' '}`, with a five-line comment explaining that the flex `gap` is visual-only and a whitespace-only flex item costs no width. The new tests can't catch it: `toHaveTextContent` (lines 47-48) normalises whitespace and asserts each span separately. — **CONFIRMED** (by JSX whitespace semantics + the sibling's own documentation of the case; not executed)

**4. `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:22` + `:50` — Major** — `variant?: 'default'` is a prop whose type admits exactly one value (which is also its default), i.e. dead API surface, while line 50 internally widens it to `'default' | 'sale'`. The JSDoc at 20-21 ("Overridden to `'sale'` automatically… callers do not need to set this themselves") reads as if `'sale'` were passable, which the type forbids. The pre-PR JSDoc was honest ("Reserved for SFCC-194's was/now treatment; only `default` is implemented today") — SFCC-194 has now landed, so the prop should be typed `'default' | 'sale'` or removed. Grep confirms no caller anywhere passes `variant`. Against typescript.md's variant/state-modelling guidance. — **CONFIRMED**

**5. `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:325-410` — Major (should-fix)** — ~90 lines of new, purely derivational price-scoping logic (a `useRef` + `useEffect` cache-write + a 55-line `useMemo` + `isPriceStale`) added inline to a 877-line component (`ProductDetail` spans 155-1032), with no unit test. The same folder already establishes the opposite pattern: `productInfo.ts` / `productInfo.test.ts` exist precisely to hold and test PDP derivation outside the page, and `overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeSection.ts` is the in-repo hook-extraction precedent. This PR added the easy half to the tested module and left the hard half (variant-scoped `getPriceData` selection, master-identity matching, deep-link fallback) untested inside the page. components.md extract-to-hook threshold + testing.md. — **CONFIRMED**

**6. `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:402` — Minor** — The `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` is unnecessary and itself emits `Unused eslint-disable directive (no problems were reported from 'react-hooks/exhaustive-deps')`. The three-line comment above it justifying the suppression documents a constraint that does not exist. — **CONFIRMED** (from the eslint run)

**7. Stale line-number claims in new comments — Minor**
- `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:87` — "*rewrites the URL's `pid` (`pages/product-detail/index.tsx` lines 328-338)*". Lines 328-338 are now the SFCC-194 comment block **this same PR inserted**; the actual `pid` rewrite (`rebuildPathWithParams(... {pid: variant?.productId})`) is at **line 430**. The PR invalidated its own reference. — **CONFIRMED**
- `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:88` — "*re-keys the `useProduct` call on line 205*". `useProduct(` is at **line 203**; 205 is `parameters: {`. — **CONFIRMED**
- Counter-check, for calibration: the same comment's claims about the base file **are** accurate — `display-price/current-price.jsx:56` is the `For screen reader…` comment and 57-66 is the `VisuallyHidden` block, exactly as stated. And `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:13`'s `assignAfter` snippet is real at `@chakra-ui/system/dist/index.js:207-213` (claimed "204-213"; `toCSSObject` starts at 203). Both are substantively right but are line-number pins into `node_modules` that any patch bump silently rots, and `dist/index.js` is unqualified by package. — Nit

**8. `pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx:45` — Minor** — Props declared as an anonymous inline intersection `ProductViewHeaderProps & { isPriceLoading?: boolean }` instead of a named `StaticProductHeaderProps`; components.md requires the props type name to match the component name. Compounding: the file's own docblock at **lines 32-33** still claims *"this keeps the prop surface exactly `ProductViewHeaderProps`, which passing `formatPrice` in would have widened"* — the PR widened it, so the comment is now false. — **CONFIRMED**

**9. `overrides/app/theme/index.test.tsx:117-121` — Minor** — This PR made an untouched comment false in two places: `ZimmProductPrice` is listed among "the three single-part atoms" (it is now multi-part, `parts: ['container','wasPrice','nowPrice']`) and "*ZimmProductPrice's sole `variants` entry is empty*" (it now has a populated `sale` variant). Tests still pass (`toBeTruthy()` only), so nothing flags it. — **CONFIRMED**

**10. Missing `Loading` story — Minor** — `isLoading` / `isPriceLoading` is a new, visually distinct state whose entire purpose is layout reservation, yet neither `zimmProductPrice/index.stories.tsx` nor `zimmProductContent/index.stories.tsx` adds a story for it (nor an `argTypes` entry), and `staticProductHeader.stories.tsx` wasn't extended either. components.md names `Loading` as the canonical example of a state warranting a named export, and `staticProductHeader.stories.tsx:147` already has `export const Loading: Story` as the in-repo precedent. — **CONFIRMED**

**11. `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:325-327` — Minor** — The file's only change is a zero-behaviour reformat of `useMemo(() => { return getPriceData(...) })` into a concise arrow, in a shared component unrelated to the ticket — against AGENTS.md's *Minimal changes*. Ironic pairing: the PR then introduces the very style it removed here at `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:938` (`renderHeader={(headerProps) => { return (...) }}`). — **CONFIRMED**

**12. `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:371-373` — Nit** — `as SfccVariant[] | undefined` is a no-op cast: `SfccVariant = any` (line 107), and the source expression is already `any`.
